findings.message: Standing from the prior review, and made worse by removing chupa/drain.py from the fence. drain() builds its control consumer internally with `from chupa.__main__ import build_control; consumer = build_control(checkout)`, after acquiring the lock. Its only inputs are checkout, dispatch, reexec, parked and before_dispatch. main() calls `pipeline(checkout)` (runner.pipeline -> prepare_pipeline -> bind(checkout, llm) -> compose_pipeline) before drain builds that consumer. Today PauseConsumer constructs the inbox itself and binds its own apply and holds. So handing ONE __main__-built inbox to both the drain control factory and compose_pipeline needs one of three changes. (a) Change drain's signature or its build_control call. drain.py is unfenced. (b) Change bind's signature. That breaks the unfenced direct `runner.bind(checkout, llm)` callers in tests/test_harvest.py, test_ladder.py, test_caps.py, test_drain_reentry.py, test_seed_successor.py, test_diagnose.py, test_harvest_orphans.py, test_seeded_phase3_06.py, test_terminal.py, test_second_problems.py, test_reject_queue.py and test_drain.py. (c) Add a defaulted Checkout field. Then the positional `Checkout(...)` constructions in the unfenced test_drain.py (pause_checkout, which LiveDrain drives through drain() directly), test_reject_queue.py and test_daemon_tasks.py carry no inbox. Either bind/build_control constructs one when it is absent, which is the forbidden missing-inbox fallback, or those suites break, and `uv run pytest -q` must stay green. The AUTHORING CLOSURE greps only direct compose_pipeline and write_active callers. It does not trace the indirect bind/build_control/Checkout reference closure that the shared-instance requirement forces.
